Calm-period test and the Smart strategy

Crypto AI · report generated 5 Oct 2026 · $1,000 starting balance · 0.1% fee per trade

In the calmest six months since 2022 (BNB, Apr–Oct 2025), simply holding won: $1,652.62 (+65.3%). The best AI strategy, Next 3 days, reached $1,398.87 (+39.9%), and the new Smart strategy only $1,077.51 (+7.8%). Over 2022–2026 on all four coins, though, Smart had the best risk-adjusted result: Sharpe 0.64 and a worst drop of −44%, against 0.38 and −76% for holding.

  • In a steady rising market the AI is too cautious. Smart was invested only about half the time and traded 117 times while BNB rose 65%.
  • In falls and choppy markets its rules pay off. Smart had the smallest worst drop in every test except the calm 2025 window.
  • Six months cannot settle which strategy is better: each Sharpe here is uncertain by about ±1.4. The 2022–2026 test (±0.46) is the one to weigh.

How the calm period was chosen

Every 6-month window since January 2022 was scanned for the one where neither BNB nor BTC had a sudden one-week fall, so the choice is a rule, not a hand-pick. Scheduled events such as Fed meetings happen every six weeks, so no window avoids them entirely; this rule excludes shock-driven crashes.

WindowBNB worst weekBTC worst weekBNB worst dropBNB change
Apr 2025 – Oct 2025 (tested)−13.9%−13.6%−13.9%+65.6%
Mar 2025 – Sep 2025−13.9%−14.2%−17.4%+44.9%
Jul 2023 – Jan 2024 (also tested)−15.7%−12.5%−21.3%+29.2%
For comparison: Jan 2026 – Jun 2026−23%–−40%−18%

Worst week = the largest fall from any 4-hour close to the lowest close in the following 7 days. Calm windows tend to be rising markets, which makes buy & hold hard to beat.

The Smart strategy

It follows your brief: buy only when confident, scale in and out instead of all-or-nothing, protect with a stop, and buy dips. Every number was fixed before the first test and not tuned afterwards.

IdeaRule
Only buy when confidentInvest by next-1-day P(up): 60%+ → 100% of the account, 57–60% → 67%, 55–57% → 33%. Below 55%, no new buying.
Don't sell all if more may comeNext-1-day P(up) ≤ 48%: sell half if next-3-days P(up) is still ≥ 55%, otherwise sell all.
Take some profitUp 10% on the position and confidence below 55% → sell half, once per position.
Stop-lossSell all 7% below the average buy price. Once up 10%, the stop moves to break-even.
Buy lowerIf next-4-hours P(up) ≤ 45% when a buy is due, place a limit order 1% below for up to 8 hours, then buy at market.
No tiny tradesChange the position only when it moves by at least 10% of the account.

Why Smart lagged here: the next-1-day probability kept crossing 48% and 55% every few candles, so Smart bought 53 times, sold all 22 times and sold half 38 times, often stepping out just before BNB moved higher. Its three stop-losses (7 Apr, 2 Aug, 22 Sep) cost $145 net, more than half of what its other sells gained ($222). It still had the smallest worst drop (−10.2%).

  • Smart cut the worst drop by roughly a third to a half on every coin (−38% to −61%, against −65% to −95% for holding).
  • Its Sharpe beat holding on ETH, BNB and SOL and matched it on BTC (0.47 vs 0.49).
  • It trades a lot: about 1,270 trades per coin and about $1,000 in fees over the period. Paying fees in BNB (0.075%) would help.
  • Next 4 hours lost 65% on average, which confirms it should only be used for timing.

How much to trust it

  • Each long-run Sharpe is uncertain by about ±0.46 per coin, so Smart's lead over Next 3 days (0.64 vs 0.56) is within the noise; its lead over holding (0.38) is clearer.
  • Smart is the ninth variant tested on this data. Its rules were fixed before any test and not tuned, but picking the best of nine still flatters the winner a little.
  • Smart's smaller worst drops are its most reliable feature: they hold on every coin and in every period except one.

Takeaways

  • In a calm rising market, holding is hard to beat: the AI steps out too often.
  • For an investor who wants smaller crashes, Smart is the most balanced choice: similar long-run returns to Next 3 days, with much smaller worst drops.
  • Possible next step: make Smart change position less often, for example by deciding once a day instead of every 4 hours. That would be a new variant, tested the same way on all periods, not tuned to the calm window.
